title: The 10 Best Cordless Routers
subtitle: Battery-powered compact and plunge routers for edges, hinges and laminate, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A cordless router is usually a compact (trim) router on a tool battery: perfect for edge profiles, hinge mortises, laminate and quick jobs away from an outlet. Most of the best sellers are bare tools for people already on a platform. We ranked 10 on rating, review volume and features (brushless motor, variable speed, soft start, LED and a battery in the box). They run from about $70 for a third-party body on DEWALT batteries to $274 for DEWALT's 2-1/4 HP plunge router.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: DEWALT 20V Max XR Cordless Router, Brushless, Tool Only (DCW600B)
products.verdict: The best-selling cordless router by a wide margin: brushless, with variable speed, soft start, electronic feedback that holds speed in the cut, an electric brake and dual LEDs. Bare tool for DEWALT 20V owners.
products.best_for: DEWALT 20V MAX owners: the cordless compact router to own.
products.skip_if: You don't own DEWALT batteries; it's tool only.
pros: 10,792 reviews at 4.8 stars; 3,000+ sold last month
Brushless with soft start and constant-speed feedback
cons: Listing showed only 7 left in stock

products.name: Milwaukee M18 FUEL Cordless Compact Router, Tool Only (2723-20)
products.verdict: Milwaukee's M18 compact router, tied for the best rating here and tied for second on sales. The Amazon listing is nearly empty: it gives 1.25 HP and nothing about speed control, so check Milwaukee's site for features.
products.best_for: Milwaukee M18 owners who want a top-rated compact router.

Guides, template and dust port included

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX XR 2-1/4 Peak HP Plunge Router, Tool Only (DCW620B)
products.verdict: A full-size cordless plunge router: 2-1/4 peak HP, a 3-position turret stop, micro-fine depth adjustment, an anti-rotation system that shuts it down if it twists, and AIRLOCK dust collection. DEWALT rates it at 256 feet of 5/8-inch roundover per DCBP520 charge.
products.best_for: Plunge cuts, mortises and big bits with no cord.

pros: Anti-rotation shutoff and turret depth stop
cons: Needs a big DEWALT battery for full output

specs.in_box: Edge guide, roller guide, dust port, 6 bits

products.verdict: A third-party brushless router that runs on DEWALT 20V batteries, with edge and roller guides and six bits, for about half the DCW600B's price. DEWALT doesn't make or warrant it.

avoid.name: HLiePiHa Cordless Compact Router for Dewalt 20V Battery, 800W Brushless, 5 Speeds (OU-10)
avoid.flag: No maker, warranty or weight listed; odd speed claim
avoid.verdict: A $37 DEWALT-battery body with almost nothing on the listing to back it up. If you're on DEWALT batteries, the DIYtoolifz costs more but lists its weight, speed range and a 5-year warranty; the DCW600B is the real thing.
reasons: The listing names no manufacturer, warranty or weight. You'd be buying a model number (OU-10) from a storefront.
It claims 5 speeds from 3,000 to 30,000 rpm. Router bits cut cleanly at 10,000 rpm and up, so the low end of that range is no use for routing, and it's an odd claim no other router here makes.
It's a third-party body on DEWALT batteries, so DEWALT doesn't warrant it, and at 3.7 stars it's the lowest-rated router we considered.

buyers_guide.q: Is a cordless router as good as a corded one?
buyers_guide.a: For compact-router work (edges, hinges, laminate), yes: the best cordless routers match a corded trim router and you skip the cord catching on the workpiece. For big bits and long dados, a corded full-size router or DEWALT's cordless plunge router has more power.
Brushless motors get more cutting per charge and hold speed better under load. On a battery tool that matters more than on a corded one.

Most brand-name cordless routers are sold bare, for people already on a platform. If you don't own batteries, a budget kit gets you running for under $85, but its batteries won't fit other brands' tools.

buyers_guide.q: What speed range do I need?
buyers_guide.a: For 1/4-inch edge bits, 20,000 to 30,000 rpm is plenty. A wider range down to 10,000 rpm lets you slow down for larger profile bits without burning.

buyers_guide.q: Can I put a cordless router in a router table?
buyers_guide.a: Compact routers can go in small trim-router tables, but battery runtime makes them a poor fit for long table sessions. A corded full-size router is the better table router.
